title: Rules and learned patterns
summary: A rule-based program follows rules written by people. A learned model finds patterns using examples. Both need testing and can make mistakes.
introduction: A rule-based program follows rules written by people. A learned model finds patterns using examples. Both need testing and can make mistakes. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A rule-based program follows rules written by people. A learned model finds patterns using examples. Both need testing and can make mistakes.

blocks.code:
Written rule: a book is long if pages > 200
Learned model: use labelled book examples to choose a pattern
Check: compare decisions with the task definition
blocks.title: Rules and learned patterns

blocks.text: The first method has an explicit threshold. The second depends on teaching examples and its learning method. Neither definition makes the result automatically correct.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Name one change in the data that could affect the learned pattern.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not call a fixed rule learned unless a learning process actually chose it.
For more detail later, use this [Artificial Intelligence further reading](https://ai4k12.org/resources/).

seo.title: AI: Rules and learned patterns
